messages:
zane: FYI we landed the 'short-request fastpath' canary in eu-central-1 at 08:02 CET. policy: requests with <=100 input tokens go to tiny-quant-v1 for the first response chunk.

prit: can you paste the high-level numbers? very curious about p99 for widgets.

zane: quick snapshot from 08:02-08:40 (5% traffic): total requests 8.1k, p50 11ms -> 7ms (-36%), p95 165ms -> 95ms (-42%), p99 490ms -> 310ms (-37%). CPU/GPU utilization on tiny hosts +12% but overall cost per token ~-26%.

nora: are we seeing any content drift? i.e. hallucination or tokenization differences with quant.

zane: ran our tiny-prompt eval (2k examples) and internal QA harness. automated checks (BLEU/QA/consistency) show no significant regressions. two narrow failure modes: precise code formatting and currency math; we added a rule to bypass fastpath when prompt contains code fence or currency symbols with explicit calc tokens.

deploy-bot: rollout: route-controller v1.14.0 -> canary(5%) (build b-20260302-07)

liu: thanks. what's the ramp schedule and rollback conditions?

zane: ramp: 5% -> 25% in 12h if p95 stays within 1.6x baseline -> 75% in 48h -> 100% in 96h. auto-rollback triggers: errors > baseline*2 for 10m OR p99 > baseline*1.8 for 5m. manual rollback if dogfood flags SLO regressions.

samira: ops-sentry, can you wire an alert for p95 and p99 regressions for this route? and include a synthetic check for code-fence prompts so we don't miss the bypass logic failing.

ops-sentry: alert rule added: fastpath/eu-central-1 p95 > baseline*1.5 -> notify @eng-oncall @eng-runtime. synthetic check scheduled every 5m for code-fence sample set.

prit: curious about Dedicated customers. does this route affect their reserved instances or billing?

zane: no changes to hardware pools. Dedicated workloads still land on customer-dedicated model groups. This feature only affects model selection within shared runtime. we've informed billing and dedicated-comm teams to ensure transparency.

nora: link to the eval artifacts? would like to skim the counterexamples before ramping.

zane: eval bundle uploaded to internal storage: https://redwood.internal/evals/shortfastpath/2026-03-02 (perm: eng-runtime). quick diff: most mismatches were whitespace/code formatting; we tightened the post-processor for code blocks.

liu: any latency variance during KV cache warmup? last month we had p99 spikes at midnight due to cache cold starts.

zane: KV path unchanged, but we added a tiny prefetch for top-50 prefixes for high-frequency routes which reduces warmup p99 by ~18% in microbench. we limited prefetch budget so memory doesn't blow up.

prit: thanks. small note for Console: please surface "fastpath adoption" in Route Analytics and a projected cost-savings estimate for customers (non-binding). product wants a line for next week's update.

zane: will add a short write-up and a dashboard tile. action items: 1) finish extended evals for code/math edge cases (nora) 2) wire console metric (zane) 3) monitor canary and ramp per schedule (ops-sentry) 4) coordinate billing note for Dedicated/enterprise (liu).

samira: great work. ping here if p99 goes funny. :rocket:
